result.summary: The image shows a wide urban intersection with multi-lane roadways and high-visibility zebra crosswalks. While a substantial concrete median refuge island is provided to break up the crossing, the overall environment is dominated by vehicle travel lanes, resulting in significant exposure for pedestrians.

hazards.name: Long Crossing Distance
hazards.description: The total width of the roadway requires pedestrians to cross multiple lanes of traffic, increasing exposure time.

hazards.name: Wide Travel Lanes
hazards.description: Generous lane widths and a lack of vertical elements near the roadway can encourage higher vehicle speeds.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the corners to reduce the crossing distance and improve the visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Leading Pedestrian Interval
interventions.description: Adjust signal timing to provide a 3-7 second head start for pedestrians before vehicles receive a green light.

interventions.title: Street Trees and Landscaping
interventions.description: Add street trees in the buffer zone to provide a physical barrier and narrow the driver's visual field to encourage slower speeds.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features narrow sidewalks that are partially obstructed by external building staircases and utility infrastructure. Parked vehicles along the curb create a continuous visual barrier between the walkway and the roadway, which lacks any marked crossing facilities.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: External metal stairs from the brick building significantly narrow the effective walking width of the sidewalk.
hazards.location_in_image: Left-center, attached to the red brick building

hazards.name: Visual Obstruction
hazards.description: A continuous line of parked cars blocks sightlines between drivers and pedestrians who might attempt to cross the street.
hazards.location_in_image: Along the curb line across the center of the image

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces near potential crossing points to improve visibility between pedestrians and motorists.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to narrow the crossing distance and prevent cars from parking too close to pedestrian access points.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crossing
interventions.description: Install a marked crosswalk with high-visibility paint and appropriate signage to provide a designated crossing point.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides and a marked bike lane, but lacks physical traffic calming or mid-block crossing infrastructure. The wide, straight roadway and extensive on-street parking create potential visibility issues and encourage higher vehicle speeds.

hazards.name: Visual obstructions from parked cars
hazards.description: Continuous parallel parking on both sides of the street obscures pedestrians from the view of oncoming drivers.
hazards.location_in_image: Along both curbs throughout the visible block.

hazards.name: Wide, straight travel lanes
hazards.description: The lack of horizontal deflection or traffic calming on this straight stretch of road may encourage speeding.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at potential crossing points to increase pedestrian visibility and reduce crossing distance.

interventions.title: Mid-block Crosswalk
interventions.description: Add a high-visibility marked crosswalk with appropriate signage to provide a designated crossing point.

interventions.title: Protected Bike Lane
interventions.description: Upgrade the painted bike lane to a protected one using bollards or planters to provide physical separation from motor vehicles.

result.summary: The street features continuous sidewalks on both sides with mature trees providing a buffer on the far side. However, the near-side walkway is partially obstructed by a large vehicle parked on the pavement, and the wide roadway layout lacks mid-block traffic calming.

hazards.name: Sidewalk Obstruction
hazards.description: A large silver minivan is parked directly on the wide sidewalk area in the foreground, forcing pedestrians to walk around it.

hazards.name: Intersection Visibility
hazards.description: Parked cars along the curb near the far intersection may block sightlines between drivers and pedestrians waiting to cross.
hazards.location_in_image: Background, right side near the traffic light

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Install curb extensions at the intersection to shorten crossing distances and improve visibility by moving pedestrians past the line of parked cars.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Remove parking spaces immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sightlines for all road users.

interventions.title: Sidewalk Delineation
interventions.description: Use bollards or planters to clearly separate the wide sidewalk area from the roadway to prevent illegal parking on the pedestrian walkway.
